new_events.claim: The UK Climate Change Committee advised on 16 September 2026 that Heathrow expansion can be consistent with UK carbon budgets and Net Zero only if the government legislates for the aviation industry to reach zero emissions by 2050 on a 'polluter pays' basis, in a pathway where industry-purchased engineered removals deliver 36% of the 2050 aviation emissions reduction (lower demand growth 24%, efficiency 20%, SAF 20%).

new_events.claim: The US National Academies' 2026 update to its marine carbon dioxide removal report series (16 September 2026) found marine CDR has advanced through field trials and private credit sales, but that major questions remain over whether it can remove CO2 at meaningful scale, how net removal can be measured and verified, and its long-term environmental effects, and that governance gaps 'directly constrain the near-term scalability' of ocean alkalinity enhancement.

new_events.claim: An Earth-system-model study posted for discussion on EGUsphere on 16 September 2026 (Tjiputra et al., not yet peer reviewed) found that tropical, Northern-Hemisphere and Southern-Hemisphere mid-latitude stratospheric aerosol injection all kept simulated overshoot warming below 2°C, but that deployment location strongly shapes side effects via the AMOC, and that legacy effects on sea-level rise and permafrost persist for centuries after SAI ends.

sources.title: Impacts and limitations of avoiding temperature overshoot with stratospheric aerosol injections (EGUsphere preprint egusphere-2026-5188)

verification.note: EGUsphere egusphere-2026-5188: discussion started 16 Sep 2026 (under review); all SAI deployments keep warming below 2C, AMOC-mediated side effects depend on location, legacy sea-level/permafrost effects for centuries.

new_events.claim: A CREA analysis for Carbon Brief (17 September 2026) found that India's CO2 emissions grew 3.7% year on year in the first half of 2026, driven by an 8% rise in steel and cement emissions (now 23% of India's CO2), even though India's power-sector CO2 was flat versus H1 2024 as clean energy met all of the 7% (63 TWh) electricity-demand growth over two years and oil and gas CO2 fell 7% year on year.

sources.title: Analysis: India's power-sector emissions flat for two years due to clean-energy surge (Carbon Brief)

verification.note: Carbon Brief 17 Sep 2026: India CO2 +3.7% H1 2026; steel+cement +8%, 23% share; power flat vs 2024 with clean energy covering 7% (63 TWh) demand growth; oil & gas -7%.

new_events.claim: CREA's China Energy and Emissions Trends August 2026 snapshot (17 September 2026) said indicators point to a broad-based decline in China's emissions in August 2026, with thermal power generation down 4% (coal power -5.2%, a second consecutive monthly fall), cement output -12%, crude steel -4% and refinery throughput -7% year on year, while thermal power capacity additions reached 50.3 GW in January-July 2026, up 20% and the highest for that period in 15 years.

verification.note: CREA snapshot 17 Sep 2026: broad-based decline; thermal -4%, coal -5.2% (second month), cement -12%, steel -4%, refining -7%; thermal additions 50.3 GW Jan-Jul, +20%, highest in 15 years.

new_events.claim: A World Weather Attribution study (17 September 2026) of the 26 August 2026 Rasuwa rock-ice avalanche and flood on the Nepal-China border (over 1,300 confirmed deaths and over 5,000 missing in Nepal) found that human-caused warming of about 1.5°C in July-August temperatures at the site (about 2°C annually) likely weakened the slope through permafrost degradation and glacier thinning, without attributing the specific collapse, and concluded the event exceeded the limits of adaptation.

sources.title: Rapid Warming in the Himalaya Exacerbates Geohazard Cascades Beyond Adaptation Limits (World Weather Attribution)

verification.note: WWA page dated 17 Sep 2026: >1,300 deaths, >5,000 missing; ~1.5C Jul-Aug and ~2C annual warming; specific collapse not attributed; beyond limits of adaptation. Guardian 17 Sep confirms.

new_events.claim: Greensand, led by INEOS Energy with Harbour Energy and Nordsøfonden, entered commercial operation on 18 September 2026 as the EU's first full-scale offshore CO2 storage site, injecting CO2 sourced primarily from Danish biomethane plants into the depleted Nini West field about 1,800 m beneath the Danish North Sea, with capacity of up to 400,000 tCO2 per year in its first phase and potential expansion to 4-8 MtCO2 per year.

current.rationale: The Mauna Loa CO2 concentration hit new records in 26H1: a 432.34 ppm monthly mean in May 2026 (+1.83 ppm on May 2025) and a 433.95 ppm daily mean on 1 May. The 10-year trend (NOAA Jan->Dec, 2016-2025) is 2.56 ppm/yr at MLO (2.53 global); its dip from 2.64 is mechanical (El Niño year 2015 left the window) and half-decade means still rose (2.51 -> 2.61 ppm/yr), so there is no structural slowdown. Year-on-year growth temporarily slowed (+1.48 to +2.26 ppm in Jan-Jun 2026), matching in direction the Met Office forecast of a slower 2026 annual-mean rise that it attributes to La Niña-like conditions, but it remains far above the 1.33-1.79 ppm/yr that IPCC 1.5°C pathways require.

current.label: Distant — 53 GtCO2e/year to eliminate
current.rationale: Global GHG emissions were 53.2 GtCO2e in 2024 and fossil CO2 hit a record in 2025, far from net zero. Net-zero targets cover 77% of global GDP, but 2025 was a year of retreat (US Paris withdrawal, banks exiting NZBA, delayed corporate targets) and most IEA net-zero pathway benchmarks are off track.

current.label: Approaching, not achieved
current.rationale: Every 2025 estimate published in 26H1 is a new record: GCB fossil CO2 38.1 GtCO2 (+1.0%), IEA energy CO2 38,082 MtCO2 (+0.4%) and Carbon Monitor fossil+industry CO2 37.2 GtCO2 (+0.7%); only GCB total CO2 dipped slightly, due to lower land-use emissions as El Niño ended. Growth has slowed to a plateau (global fossil power generation fell 0.2%, China and India flat), but China's CO2 rose 2% in Q1 2026 and the IEA expects the shock-driven 2026 oil-demand fall to rebound above the 2025 level in 2027, so the peak is not definitively behind us. Caveat: the milestone covers all greenhouse gases, but no global 2025 total-GHG estimate was published within 26H1, so CO2 estimates serve as the proxy.

current.label: Under pressure
current.rationale: 2024 was the first calendar year to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial (WMO 1.55°C), though the long-term Paris metric remains ~1.3-1.4°C. WMO gives 70% odds the 2025-2029 average also exceeds 1.5°C, and the 1.5°C carbon budget is virtually exhausted.
